title: Safe Function Declaration & Hoisting Sandbox
concept: ES6 Annex B Block Scoping for Function Declarations
problemStatement: In ES6+, function declarations inside `if` blocks are block-scoped. Implement `evaluateBlockFunctions(condition, trueFnName, falseFnName)` that executes a simulated block-scoped environment and returns which function is accessible outside the block vs inside.
interviewTrap: In legacy ES5 / non-strict mode, function declarations in blocks were hoisted out into function scope, overwriting each other. In strict mode, they are strictly block scoped.

testCases.name: Functions are scoped and execute deterministically
testCases.testFn: const r1 = evaluateBlockFunctions(true); const r2 = evaluateBlockFunctions(false); return typeof r1.insideResult === 'string' && typeof r2.insideResult === 'string';

details.name: Functions are scoped and execute deterministically

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: A Hoisting & TDZ Sandbox safely evaluates dynamic code strings containing arbitrary var/let/const and function declarations, capturing TDZ violations and hoisting behaviors without crashing the parent execution context.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Construct an isolated execution scope using `new Function()` with trapped globals.
Instrument the code or catch runtime `ReferenceError`s resulting from premature access to uninitialized bindings.
Distinguish between standard undeclared variables (`ReferenceError: x is not defined`) and TDZ access errors (`ReferenceError: Cannot access 'x' before initialization`).
Return structured diagnostics detailing hoisted identifiers, TDZ traps encountered, and final return values.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: Function declarations in blocks (Annex B.3.3) have complex legacy hoisting semantics. Top-level function declarations are fully hoisted with their implementation during the Creation phase. `new Function` creates a fresh global-like script context that prevents local scope pollution.

complexity.time: O(E) execution time of evaluated code snippet.

edgeCasesHandled: Allowing hoisted function calls before declaration line.
Handling syntax errors vs runtime TDZ reference errors distinctly.

specifications: ECMA-262 Annex B.3.3 Block-Level Function Declarations Web Legacy Compatibility
ECMA-262 §19.2.1.1 Function ( p1, p2, … , pn, body ) (Dynamic function evaluation)
verifiedRules: Function declarations are hoisted with function body definition.
TDZ exceptions are distinct runtime ReferenceErrors originating from uninitialized environment slots.
